title: SarDomain
description: SAR acquisition geometry and imaging modes. The single most important fact encoded here: SAR is SIDE-LOOKING. A target directly beneath the satellite is NOT imageable. Access therefore requires an incidence angle inside the sensor's valid band, a permitted look side, a squint within steering limits, and a slant range inside bounds — all four, simultaneously. Anything that models this as a nadir-pointing sensor is modelling a different instrument.

ImagingMode.description: SPOTLIGHT: small area, finest resolution, longest dwell — the beam is steered to stare at one spot as the satellite passes. STRIPMAP: fixed beam, medium swath and resolution, dwell proportional to along-track length. SCAN: widest swath, coarsest resolution, shortest dwell per unit area. Mode selection interacts with both feasibility and plan value, which is why it is on the request rather than chosen silently.

LookSide.description: Which side of the ground track the beam points, in the along-track direction of travel. Some satellites and modes are constrained to one side; a target reachable only on the forbidden side is simply not accessible on that pass.

LookSideConstraint.description: A customer-side preference or restriction. ANY means the planner may use either side.

TleStaleness.description: Classification of tle_age_hours against configured thresholds. TLEs decay in accuracy — a days-old TLE drifts enough to move a computed access window by seconds to minutes, which is the difference between a valid plan and an unflyable one. FRESH: feasibility results are trusted. AGING: results are published with a flag and surfaced in the UI. STALE: feasibility REFUSES to compute and emits feasibility.failed.v1 with reason TLE_STALE. Refusing is the correct behaviour; producing a confidently wrong answer is not.

tle_epoch.description: Epoch of the TLE used, decoded from the element set itself — not the time we fetched it.

tle_age_hours.description: Hours between tle_epoch and the time feasibility ran. Carried on the event so that a stale result is auditable after the fact, not just filterable at the time.

TleReference.description: Provenance of the orbital data behind a feasibility result. Present on every opportunity batch so that any computed window can be traced back to the exact element set that produced it.

incidence_angle_deg.description: Angle between the radar line of sight and the local vertical at the target. The sensor's valid band is configuration, not contract (default 15-45 degrees); the schema permits 0-90 so that a differently-specified sensor does not require a schema version. Values outside the configured band are filtered by feasibility and never appear on an opportunity.

squint_angle_deg.description: Angle of the beam fore (positive) or aft (negative) of broadside. Zero is pure broadside. Bounded by the sensor's steering limit; SPOTLIGHT uses the widest range because staring at a fixed spot during a pass necessarily sweeps squint.

slant_range_km.description: Line-of-sight distance from satellite to target. Bounded below by the sensor's minimum range and above by the link budget.

elevation_angle_deg.description: Elevation of the satellite above the target's local horizon. The complement of incidence for a spherical Earth; carried separately because the ellipsoidal computation makes them not quite complementary, and rounding that away would be exactly the sort of quiet error this project's golden tests exist to catch.

ground_azimuth_deg.description: Azimuth from target to satellite ground position, degrees clockwise from true north. Used by the frontend to draw the look direction.

roll_angle_deg.description: Spacecraft roll required to achieve this incidence angle. This is the input to slew_time(a, b): two acquisitions with very different roll angles need time between them for the attitude manoeuvre plus settling, which is what turns naive interval scheduling into scheduling with sequence-dependent setup times.

AccessGeometry.description: The four-plus-one geometric quantities that decide whether an acquisition is physically possible, plus the roll angle that decides whether it is reachable from the previous one.

SensorModeParameters.description: Per-mode sensor characteristics. Stored in a JSONB column because the fields genuinely differ per mode and will keep changing as the geometry model is refined — one of the four documented JSONB cases in ADR-0004.

AcquisitionConstraints.description: Customer-supplied narrowing of the acceptable geometry. Every field is optional; omitting all of them means the sensor's own limits apply. Constraints can only narrow, never widen — a customer cannot request an incidence angle the sensor does not support.
